messages:
alice_support: Hey team — our mobile backend started getting 401s from Redwood after a deploy to Cloudflare Workers. No code change to auth layer, just moved the request through a worker proxy. Seen by a few users.

alice_support: Example curl that fails:```
curl -i -H "Authorization: ApiKey ABC123xyz==" https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

alice_support: Response: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized {"error":"invalid_api_key"}`

bob_support: Thanks — can you paste the raw request headers from the worker (what the worker actually sends to upstream)? Often CF Workers helpers mutate headers or encode values.

alice_support: Pasting worker snippet and headers we see going out:```
// worker
const headers = new Headers();
headers.set('Authorization', `ApiKey ${encodeURIComponent(SECRET_KEY)}`);
fetch(UPSTREAM, { method: 'POST', headers, body });
```
Outgoing headers captured on our side:```
Authorization: ApiKey ABC123xyz%3D%3D
Content-Type: application/json
```

bob_support: Aha — the header value is percent-encoded (`%3D` = `=`). Redwood expects the raw key bytes (no URL-encoding). Our token parser treats that as a malformed key and returns invalid_api_key.

sam_engineer: Confirming — if the Authorization header contains characters that don't match our key regex (we allow [A-Za-z0-9_\-+=/]+, length check), percent-encoded sequences will fail validation.

alice_support: Workaround deployed: removed encodeURIComponent and now worker sets raw string. Re-tested curl and app — success: 200/OK.

alice_support: Example fixed code:```
const headers = new Headers();
headers.set('Authorization', `ApiKey ${SECRET_KEY}`);
fetch(UPSTREAM, { method: 'POST', headers, body });
```

maria_support: Filing this as an internal KB note for common Cloudflare Workers pitfall (helpers that encode headers). Also adding a short repro for support:```
# repro steps
1) Deploy a worker that uses `encodeURIComponent` when setting Authorization header.
2) Send request -> observe `401 invalid_api_key` from Redwood.
3) Remove encoding -> observe `200`.
```

bob_support: Thanks. Can we add a small validation message in support replies: when customers hit invalid_api_key while proxying through workers/proxies, ask them to dump raw header bytes (or run `curl -v` on the worker to show what actually reaches Redwood).

sam_engineer: Filing a brief engineering note: consider logging a non-sensitive fingerprint of the presented key on 401 (e.g., first 6 chars + length) to help debug encoding/truncation issues without exposing secrets. Escalation ID: ENG-5642.

deploy-bot: deploy accepted: workers/fix-auth-encoding @alice_support

alice_support: Deployed fix to prod and rollback of a helper lib in canary. Users report restored service. Marking resolved for now, will follow up if regressions. :tada:

maria_support: Closing thread, adding to KB under "401 invalid_api_key — header encoding/truncation".
